**Ch 012 draft — candidate issues:**

The Mapple sermon is very faithfully compressed. The one structural seam worth examining:

> "How being an anointed pilot-prophet, and bidden by the Lord to sound those unwelcome truths in the ears of a wicked Nineveh, Jonah, appalled at the hostility he should raise, fled from his mission…"

In the source this sentence is preceded by: *"How gladly would I come down from this mast-head… and listen… while some one of you reads me that other and more awful lesson which Jonah teaches to me, as a pilot of the living God."* The draft keeps the "I have read ye… the lesson that Jonah teaches to all sinners… and still more to me" but then launches directly into "How being an anointed pilot-prophet…" The "How" clause is a fragment — it functions in the source as the content of the lesson Mapple wishes someone would read *to him*, introduced by the preceding "How gladly would I… listen while some one reads me…" The draft cuts the framing clause ("How gladly would I come down… listen while some one reads me *that other and more awful lesson*") and leaves only the "How being…" subordinate clause, which is now missing its governing matrix clause. A reader encounters a subordinate "How being…" clause with no main verb directing it.

**Ch 013 draft — candidate issues:**

> "I would remonstrate; but he silenced me by pouring them into my pockets."

Source: "I was going to remonstrate." Draft changed this to "I would remonstrate" — this is a minor tense shift, not a structural break.

> "Thus, then, in our hearts' honeymoon, lay I and Queequeg — a cosy, loving pair."

The source has a transition paragraph before this: "But we did not go to sleep without some little chat. How it is I know not; but there is no place like a bed for confidential disclosures…" The draft keeps "How it is I know not; but there is no place like a bed for confidential disclosures between friends. Thus, then…" — the "Thus, then" resolves fine.

No structural breaks found in Ch 013 beyond the authorized-cut residues.
